headline: The new password reminder exposes passwords and stops existing customers from signing in.
what_changed: Customers can now request an email that claims to remind them of their password.
New customer passwords are kept in readable form instead of protected form.
Existing customer sign-ins will no longer work after this change.

risks.title: Passwords are stored in readable form
risks.explanation: Anyone who gains access to the customer database can read every new password. People often reuse passwords, so this can expose accounts beyond this product. Restore one-way password protection before publishing.

risks.title: Existing customers cannot sign in
risks.explanation: Passwords saved before this change were stored in a protected scrambled form. The new sign-in check only accepts a readable stored password, so those customers will be rejected. Keep support for the existing protected form, then safely update it after successful sign-in.

risks.title: Password emails expose customer secrets
risks.explanation: For newly created accounts, the password reminder sends the actual password by email. Anyone who accesses a customer's mailbox or a copied email can take over the account. Send a short-lived, single-use reset link instead.

questions_for_developer: Can you replace the password reminder with a short-lived, single-use reset link and restore protected password storage?
How will existing customers keep signing in after the password storage change?
good_news: The password reminder avoids confirming whether an email address has an account.
